name: Kayleigh — 75 hours, mostly ridge, wants to fly comps next year
summary: Around 75 hours total with under 10 of them thermic, on her mid-B for about 30 hours. Climbs in wide turns and loses the core, right about half the time on reading a day, trying to react when it's bumpy but it isn't automatic. Hasn't practised collapses. Goes when her friends go, launches rather than stand down, and has had a few near misses she can't explain. She expects a better wing to handle turbulence better than hers does, and wants to be flying long cross-countries and competitions.
why_this_persona: The clearly-not-ready case, and the one that checks the gates stack sensibly rather than piling on. Three gates fire at once, which is exactly the cap on displayed gate reasons, so this is the persona to read for whether a Not yet with several reasons still lands as a useful result rather than a telling-off. Her ambitions are entirely legitimate and must be treated as such — the only thing the rubric objects to is the groundwork underneath them.

notes: Computed skills 45.5, psychological 30.7, total 38.8, no bonus. Her psychological score is also below the Not yet floor of 35, but gates short-circuit, so no rule is reported — only the three gates.

THREE GATES, which is exactly gate_behaviour.max_gate_reasons_shown. That is deliberate coverage: this is the one persona that tests whether a stacked Not yet reads acceptably. A reviewer should read all three messages together and check they don't repeat each other or pile on. The thermic-hours message is actionable, the equipment message is factual about the class, and the ambition message explicitly defends the ambition.

'aspirational_rather_than_demonstrated' must NOT fire. She answers 'I've wondered, but I couldn't point to a particular flight' on wing_limiting_evidence, which is NOT the 'not really' band that gate requires. It still scores 0.4 and would block Ready, and it still triggers the 'wing_hasnt_limited_you_yet' suggestion — but the cap is reserved for the clearer answer. A scorer that widens that gate to the second band will produce four gates here.

'post_collapse_support' must NOT fire. Its triggers are a mishandled collapse or a frightening incident, and hers are 'never' and 'a few I can't explain'. The right suggestion for her unexplained near misses is 'debrief_habit', which is a different action.

'expectation_research' must NOT fire: its trigger bands are 'not sure' and 'not a huge difference', and hers is 'it'll handle turbulence better' — which is a factually wrong expectation rather than an absent one, so it gets 'motivation_reframe_equipment_fix' instead. Those two suggestions share no topic and must never both appear for the same answer.

Her ambitions are longer_xc and competitions, which is what 'ambition_without_readiness' needs alongside a skills score under 55. Compare persona 05, who ticks longer_xc with skills at 70.8 and is NOT gated by it, and persona 01, who ticks longer_xc with skills at 96 and reaches Ready. The three together pin the rule that ambition never costs a band on its own.
